title: Adjacent context propagation probe notebook
content:
Purpose:
- Quick brain-dump + working spec for an "adjacent context" propagation feature.
- Goal: enable short-lived cross-request context transfer (soft affinity) without full session pinning. Useful for conversational handoffs between related requests, multi-device handover, and low-cost micro-conversations stitched over separate API calls.

Motivation / pain we hit:
- Clients split a user flow into many independent generation calls (search + refine + summarize). They re-send repeated context; waste tokens and latency.
- Full session affinity/pinning is heavy: stateful infra implications, storage, billing semantics.
- Existing KV-cache is single-request prefix cache, not cross-request adjacency-aware.

Design goals (constraints):
1) Lightweight: propagate compact context pointers / deltas, not full transcript.
2) Ephemeral: default TTL small (seconds->minutes), evictable.
3) Privacy-safety: honor redaction flags and tenant boundaries.
4) Cost-aware: optional sampling, clients opt-in.
5) Compatible with hosted and private deployments (config knobs for on-prem stricter defaults).

High-level idea:
- Introduce an "adjacent context" concept: small artifacts (anchors) created by requests that can be referenced by subsequent requests. Artifacts are vectorized fingerprints + small metadata + optional compressed snippet.
- Runtime stores artifacts in a per-tenant adjacent-store (in-memory with spill to fast KV). Each artifact has adjacency_score, TTL, visibility tags.
- New request may pass adjacency_hints: list of artifact ids + match policy. Runtime may merge top-K artifact content into tokenized prefix or use retrieval-by-vector to inject retrieved segments.

API sketch (client-facing):
1) Response-level hint: server returns hint token in generation responses when it creates an artifact.
- Response header: X-Adj-Artifact: adj://<tenant>/<artifact_id>?score=0.72
- Body metadata example (JSON string): "adj_artifact: {id: "adj_01c9e", score: 0.72, excerpt_tokens: 28, ttl_s: 300}"

2) Request-level affinity: client includes adjacency_hints in subsequent requests.
- POST /v1/generate
  headers: Authorization, Content-Type
  body: {"model": "redwood-large-1", "prompt": "<user prompt>", "adjacency": {"hints": ["adj://tenant/adj_01c9e"], "policy": "merge_if_relevant", "max_merge_tokens": 64}}

Adjacency config keys (runtime + per-tenant overrides):
- adjacency.enabled = true|false
- adjacency.default_ttl_s = 300
- adjacency.max_artifact_size_tokens = 256
- adjacency.max_hits_per_request = 4
- adjacency.merge_policy = ["merge_always","merge_if_relevant","vector_rerank_only"]
- adjacency.relevance_threshold = 0.45  # cosine-based for vector-match
- adjacency.prioritize_by = ["recency","adjacency_score","explicit_score"]

Artifact shape (stored):
- id: string (adj_...)
- created_at: iso
- created_by_call_id: string
- excerpt: compressed string (optional)
- vector: base64 or vector shard id (for retrieval)
- token_count: int
- adjacency_score: float (0..1)
- ttl_s: int
- visibility_tags: list (e.g., "session-local", "tenant-public")
- redact_flags: list (e.g., "pii")

Note: the artifact shape above is runtime internal. We only expose id + score to clients unless tenant allows excerpt.

Runtime merge strategies (sketch):
- merge_always: prepend selected excerpts directly to prompt (bounded by max_merge_tokens). Fast, but risk of irrelevant context.
- merge_if_relevant: run a lightweight reranker (vector similarity over prompt embedding vs artifact vectors). Only merge if score > relevance_threshold.
- vector_rerank_only: no token injection; instead embed incoming prompt and rerank artifact candidates to influence routing/score. For models with retrieval-augmented fusion.

Eviction and lifecycle:
- LRU + TTL. Keep per-tenant memory footprint under adjacency.memory_limit_mb.
- A background compaction job consolidates small similar artifacts (merge criteria: overlap_ratio > 0.7 and same visibility).
- Auditable deletion: artifacts with redact_flags must be scrubbed and replaced with tombstones that deny further retrieval.

Security / privacy considerations:
- Default: only artifact ids and scores returned to client. Excerpts only if tenant config allows and content passes a sanitization pipeline.
- Cross-tenant isolation enforced: artifact ids include tenant prefix, runtime verifies.
- KMS/HSM: optionally encrypt excerpt blobs at rest.

Telemetry / metrics to emit (per request):
- adj.artifacts_created (count)
- adj.artifacts_returned (count)
- adj.merges_performed (count)
- adj.merge_tokens_consumed (tokens)
- adj.relevance_score_distribution (histogram)
- adj.safety_triggers (count)  // times content redacted/refused
- adj.cache_hit_rate, adj.evictions

Experiment matrix (A/B ideas):
- A: no adjacency (baseline)
- B: merge_if_relevant with threshold 0.4
- C: merge_always up to 128 tokens
- D: vector_rerank_only + rerank weight 0.2 in prompt scoring
Metrics to measure: end-to-end latency, tokens consumed, user-perceived success (via client-provided signal), failure rate, hallucination regression (eval set).

Example flow (ASCII):
User: "find good dinner spots near me" -> server creates artifact adj_abc (excerpt: 2 bullets, vector)
Client: subsequent refactor call: "now summarize top option" with adjacency hint adj_abc -> runtime reranks and merges top excerpt -> model returns summary faster (less prompt tokens).

Open questions / tradeoffs (todo list):
- Billing semantics: are artifact-injected tokens billable to client on merge? (Probably yes; but we should include clear token attribution in observability.)
- Long-term persistence: should we allow TTL extension on explicit refresh? risk: stale PII.
- What privacy labels should block excerpt export? (SSN, emails, addresses?). Integrate with existing redaction classifier.
- Multi-device handoff: artifact can be used from mobile-to-web; need secure short-lived HMAC on artifact id to avoid spoofing.
- How to gracefully degrade when vector store is cold or down? (fallback to id-only, or bypass).

Implementation notes (runtime):
- Store: in-memory LRU with Rocks-backed spill (per-tenant namespace). Quick vector shard lookup for top-K.
- Index: FAISS or small ANN library tuned for short vectors. Keep vector dim small (~128) to keep retrieval cheap.
- Reranker: cheap dot-product on warmed embeddings (use cached prompt embedding or compute on request).
- Observation: merging is easiest for small-excerpt scenarios (faq-like). For long transcripts, merge leads to prompt explosion; prefer vector_rerank_only.

Next steps / action items:
- Prototype: Rohit + Jia to build small in-memory service with two endpoints: create_artifact, retrieve_candidates. 2-week spike.
- Eval harness: Noah to define small set of 50 microflows to measure token savings and regression risk.
- Security review: add item to INF-8421 to evaluate redact classifier thresholds.
- UX: consider including small client SDK helper to accept X-Adj-Artifact header and reattach hints automatically.

Notes-to-self (small brainstorm):
- Could use sequence-level fingerprints instead of full text snippets (e.g., rolling 64-token sha256 blocks) to avoid exposing text but still allow fuzzy match.
- Consider adding an optional crediting header so that adjacent artifact creator gets a share (for billing clarity when multiple clients interact).
- For private deployments, default TTL should be 0 (off) and opt-in via tenant flag.

Rough timeline:
- Week 0-2: prototype + toy client SDK
- Week 3-4: run experiments against 50 workflows, collect metrics
- Week 5-6: iterate safety gate and redact integration
- Week 8: design doc for eng + security review

Scratch/Examples (small JSON snippets as examples, verbatim):
- Create artifact response metadata:
  "adj_artifact: {
    \"id\": \"adj_01c9e\",
    \"score\": 0.72,
    \"excerpt_tokens\": 18,
    \"ttl_s\": 300
  }"

- Client request with adjacency hints:
  {"model":"redwood-large-1","prompt":"Summarize the top result","adjacency":{"hints":["adj://acme/adj_01c9e"],"policy":"merge_if_relevant","max_merge_tokens":64}}

-- end of notebook --

Unresolved: decide on default per-tenant memory_limit_mb and safe excerpt threshold. Put as follow-up in INF-8421.
